marks.gloss_en: דההוא זוגא דרבנן דאשתכור בהלולא דבריה דרבי יהושע בן לוי... אמר: כדאי הוא רבי שמעון לסמוך עליו בשעת הדחק -- the ruling was inferred from what he told the pair who slept past dawn (no `maaseh` support kind exists; kind svara)
R' Yehoshua ben Levi [to the pair who slept past dawn]: R' Shimon is worthy to rely on in an hour of pressure
לא, לעולם יממא הוא, והאי דקרו ליה ליליא -- דאיכא אינשי דגנו בההיא שעתא: it is day; it is called night only because some people are still asleep (= p_kodem_hanetz_yom, p_karu_leih_laila)
the span just before sunrise is in truth day
R' Acha b. R' Chanina in R' Yehoshua ben Levi's name: the halakha follows R' Shimon who said it in R' Akiva's name (placement 2: the sunrise baraita)
Rav Yitzchak bar Yosef: R' Yehoshua ben Levi's ruling (as R' Acha b. R' Chanina transmits it) was not said explicitly but was inferred
נאמר כאן בלילה הזה ונאמר להלן ועברתי בארץ מצרים בלילה הזה -- as there until midnight, so here until midnight
לא קשיא: הא רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, הא רבי עקיבא -- the mishnah follows R' Elazar ben Azarya (until midnight), the baraita R' Akiva (= p_matnitin_reba, p_baraita_rakiva)
this [the mishnah] accords with R' Elazar ben Azarya
תניא נמי הכי: הוציאך ה' אלהיך ממצרים לילה -- they left by day, so the verse teaches that the redemption began in the evening
the baraita: 'brought you out of Egypt at night' -- did they leave at night? they left by day (Num 33:3)! rather, it teaches that the redemption began for them in the evening
ורמינהי: קריאת שמע ערבית והלל בלילי פסחים ואכילת פסח מצותן עד שיעלה עמוד השחר -- the baraita has the Pesach eaten until dawn, against the mishnah's omission
the baraita: the evening Shema may be recited until dawn

the mishnah does not list eating the Paschal lamb among the mitzvot that run until dawn -- so, per the mishnah, it is eaten only until midnight (the value the sugya supplies through R' Elazar ben Azarya)
R' Akiva: it was already said 'in haste' (Ex 12:11) -- the Paschal lamb is eaten until the hour of haste
(entertained) one might think the Paschal lamb is eaten by day, like other offerings
'THAT night' comes to exclude another night: it is eaten on that night and not on another night
R' Elazar ben Azarya derives 'not on another night' from 'you shall not leave any of it until morning' (Ex 12:10)
R' Akiva needs הזה because from that verse alone one would say 'morning' means the second morning
R' Elazar could say: every [unqualified] 'morning' is the first morning
the dispute of these tannaim (R' Elazar ben Azarya / R' Akiva) is the dispute of those tannaim (R' Eliezer / R' Yehoshua on Deut 16:6)
'in the evening' (Deut 16:6) -- you slaughter
all agree: when Israel were redeemed from Egypt they were redeemed only in the evening -- 'the Lord your God brought you out of Egypt at night' (Deut 16:1)
what they disagree about is the hour of haste
R' Akiva holds: 'haste' is the haste of Israel
the school of R' Yannai: 'na' (Ex 11:2) is nothing but a word of request

ורבן גמליאל מי קאמר עד חצות דקתני ולא זו בלבד אמרו? -- does Rabban Gamliel hold 'until midnight', that he should say 'and not only this did THEY say'? the wording makes him a party to a limit he rejects
הכי קאמר להו רבן גמליאל לבניה -- read it: even on the Rabbis' view the mitzva runs till dawn, and their 'until midnight' is a fence (= p_hachi_kaamar)
the clause is to be read thus: Rabban Gamliel told his sons that even according to the Rabbis who say 'until midnight', the mitzva runs until dawn
the mishnah (Rabban Gamliel's clause): 'and not only this did they say, but [wherever the Sages said until midnight, the mitzva is until dawn]'

ועד השתא לא שמיע להו הא דרבן גמליאל?! -- had his own sons not heard, until now, that he permits the Shema after midnight? then they could not have been asking what the narrative seems to say they asked

הכי קאמרי ליה -- they were not asking his view; they asked whether the Rabbis dispute him (so the many prevail) or agree and fence, and he answered: they agree, you are obligated, and 'until midnight' is a fence (= p_hachi_kaamri)
what they asked was: do the Rabbis dispute you, or do they agree with you and say 'until midnight' only as a fence?
the mishnah: Rabban Gamliel's sons came [late] from a wedding hall and asked him whether they might still recite the Shema
